title: How to Zoom OUT (for a cutscene)

posts.author: Cid
posts.body:
Hello!
I've poked around the ScreenZoom plugin from the MZ Resources and looked at MultiTweaks camera zoom functions but neither of them seem to offer the ability to zoom
out
, only in, because you cannot enter values LESS than 1 (normal zoom) in the zoom parameters.
For cutscene purposes, ideally what I'm hoping to do is start with a broader view of the action and zoom in on your playable character in the crowd to begin gameplay.
Is there something I'm missing with any of these plugins or is there an alternative known plugin that offers this feature?
I
may
be able to bodge this by exporting a PNG of the battlefield as a parallax, zooming in on
that
and attempting to switch seamlessly to the real map to initiate gameplay. But that might not work correctly and if it does I think I'll be locked out of having anything animating during the camera movement, which isn't ideal. I'm hoping to find a more obvious solution that I'm not seeing.

Not entirely sure why you'd need a plugin here. have you tried the script call for it? it lets you zoom out just fine if you give it a decimal.
taken straight from
RPG Maker MV / MZ Script Call List
This Script Call list applies to both RPG Maker MV and RPG Maker MZ. Link here to see the entire list.    Supplementary Material for RPG Maker MZ: https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/rpg-maker-mz-script-call-reference.122501/  Have fun eventing~
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Code:
var x = Graphics.width / 2;
var y = Graphics.height / 2;
var scale = 2;
var duration = 5 * 60;
$gameScreen.startZoom(x, y, scale, duration)

Unfortunately, in this case there's a slight hiccup, unless there's a step I'm missing! Using this call doesn't actually expand the scope of what's being rendered, it just zooms out on what's there when the zoom starts, meaning I get black borders around what's just a shrinking square of visuals. What I'm hoping for is a broader view of everything before zooming in to regular scale!
Is there something I can do about the... is it called 'draw distance' in 2D?
